newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslav parliament elects central bank governor.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslav parliament elects central bank governor.

text.p: Yugoslavia's parliament on Thursday elected Serbian finance minister Dusan Vlatkovic as central bank governor, filling the post which has been vacant for more than a year.
Vlatkovic, 59, a close ally of Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic, was elected at separate sessions by both chambers of the Socialist-led parliament.
The Montenegrin People's Party and Serbian Radical Party, the only opposition present at the sessions, voted against the nomination submitted by Yugoslav President Zoran Lilic.
They held Vlatkovic directly responsible for Yugoslavia's 1992-1994 hyperinflation and said he was inappropriate to head an independent monetary institution such as the National Bank of Yugoslavia.
Serbia and the much smaller Montenegro are the only remaining republics in the Yugoslav federation.
Vlatkovic, finance minister in the Serbian government since 1994, led the central bank of the former Yugoslavia from 1986 to 1992.
The central bank governorship has been vacant since May 1996, when the Socialists ousted 78-year-old Dragoslav Avramovic over his maverick stands.
Avramovic gained fame for halting the country's inflation of 60 percent a day in 1994 and his persistent refusal to print money, which put him at loggerheads with the ruling party.
The NBY Deputy Governor Bozidar Gazivoda, appointed Yugoslav finance minister in March this year, has been acting as central bank governor since then.
